title: Capacity Pools, Scaling Contracts, and Graceful Degradation PRD
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Define interfaces, economics, and operational rules for capacity pools that support contracted scaling credits and deterministic graceful degradation policies for Dedicated customers. This PRD covers scaling contracts (burst credits and decaying windows), per-tenant throttling/backpressure, and automated graceful-degradation paths when capacity is constrained.
background: Customers on Dedicated need predictable throughput and occasional headroom for traffic spikes. Existing reserved pools provide base capacity but lack a standardized, enforceable mechanism for temporary overage (bursts) tied to contracts. When demand exceeds available capacity we currently surface opaque throttling to customers which leads to poor UX and costly incident handling. This initiative creates a contract-backed scaling credit model, clear tenant throttling mechanics, and deterministic graceful degradation behaviors to preserve core SLOs.
objectives: Provide a contract-driven burst mechanism (scaling credits) that allows predictable overage with accounting and billing tie-ins
Implement deterministic graceful degradation that favors high-priority tenants and preserves latency SLOs for critical routes
Expose tenant-level visibility (credits balance, burst history, degradation events) in Console and API for troubleshooting and billing reconciliation
Minimize manual oncall interventions by automating safe fallback behaviors and runbook-triggered alerts
success_metrics: % of spike events where latency SLOs for high-priority routes are preserved >= 95%
Reduction in customer incident pages related to opaque throttling by 60% within 3 months of rollout
Billing accuracy: burst usage reported in Console matches billing CSV within 0.5%
Time-to-restore (full-ramp after capacity reclaimed) median < 5 minutes for automated fallback paths
user_stories: As a platform admin, I want to provision a Dedicated tenant with a scaling contract (base RUs and burst credits) so the tenant can handle short spikes without manual capacity adds
As an SRE, I want the system to automatically degrade non-critical routes and preserve core generation routes under sustained overload so customer-facing features remain available
As a customer success engineer, I want visibility into a customer's credit balance, recent burst events, and applied degradation policies so I can explain behavior during an incident
As a billing engineer, I want burst usage events exported to our billing pipeline with clear timestamps and contract IDs so charges are auditable
functional_requirements: Define a scaling credit model: credits are purchased/allocated per billing period, each credit equals N tokens or request units. Credits decay on a configurable window (e.g., 30d) and support partial refunds on contract changes
Implement a pool controller that enforces base capacity allocations and consults credit balances to allow requests above base up to guarantee: base + min(burst_limit, credits_available)
Support tenant priority tiers and route-level prioritization so degradation can be applied at route, model, or token granularity
Graceful degradation ruleset: cascade of actions (disable low-priority routes -> reduce max tokens -> switch to smaller model variant) with pluggable order and rollback windows
Console APIs: view credit balance, recent bursts, projected exhaustion date, and apply one-off emergency credits via Console and API
Billing integration: produce burst usage events with contract_id, tenant_id, start_ts, end_ts, credits_consumed, and rate_multiplier
Telemetry: emit events for credit consumption, degradation activations, and fallback rollbacks with correlation IDs for request traces
Safety: automatic hard cap when credits exhausted with configurable soft-window warnings before enforcement
non_goals: Not covering multi-tenant hardware oversubscription strategies (this is handled by infra autoscaler iterations)
Not replacing existing per-tenant SLAs or legal contract negotiation flows
Not implementing a full marketplace for credits purchase in this phase (manual ops and billing integration only)
acceptance_criteria: A tenant can be provisioned with a contract specifying base capacity and a numeric burst credit balance via API and Console
During controlled load tests, requests above base capacity consume credits and are routed until credits are exhausted; consumed credits are recorded and visible in Console within 60s
When credits are exhausted, the system executes configured graceful-degradation policy in the specified order and latency for protected routes remains within SLO 95th percentile window
Burst usage records are produced and ingested by billing pipeline test harness and reconcile within 0.5% of simulated usage
Telemetry events for degradation start/stop include traceable correlation IDs and appear in observability dashboards within 2 minutes
Admin can issue emergency credits via Console and the change takes effect for new requests within 30s without requiring tenant agent restarts
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal beta): implement model and API, enable for internal test tenants and run synthetic spike scenarios (2 weeks)
Phase 2 (pilot customers): enable for 3 pilot Dedicated customers with agreed contracts; collect telemetry and iterate on degradation rules (4 weeks)
Phase 3 (gradual opt-in): Console toggle for eligible customers, enable billing integration and billing CSV exports (2 weeks)
Phase 4 (default offering): expose scaling contracts as a purchasable option in Sales flow and enable self-serve for select SKUs (post-pilot)
Rollback plan: global feature toggle + per-tenant disable; immediate disable triggers expiration of pending credits but preserves recorded events for billing reconciliation
open_questions: What is the canonical unit for credits (tokens, request-units, or compute-seconds)? Decision required from SRE and Billing
Should credits be refundable or transferable between tenant sub-accounts? Legal and Billing need to confirm
How should we price emergency one-off credits vs purchased contract credits? Sales and Finance need input
What guardrails are required for multi-region Dedicated tenants to prevent cross-region capacity leakage?
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Misaccounted credits causing customer billing disputes. Mitigation: end-to-end test harness, reconcile daily snapshots, provide CSV audit export
Risk: Degradation rules incorrectly impact critical customer flows. Mitigation: pilot with opt-in customers and conservative default policy that only affects routes marked low-priority
Risk: Latency spikes during policy transitions. Mitigation: implement phased transition (per-request leaky-bucket) and measure in canary before full rollout
Risk: Abuse of burst credits by noisy tenants. Mitigation: per-tenant rate caps, anomaly detection, and contract terms specifying fair use
